summary: Describes how to create a conference using SIP URI-list services. A user agent client gives a conference server the initial list of participants by including a URI list in the INVITE request. The server can then invite everyone on the list. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: To start a group call, you hand the call organizer a list of people to ring. This describes how to include that list in your call request.

questions: how to invite multiple participants in sip
how to create a sip conference with a uri list
what does copycontrol bcc mean in sip
subtitle: How a SIP client can create a conference and hand the server its first guest list in a single INVITE.

tldr.problem: Creating an ad hoc SIP conference and then adding participants takes several steps, but some environments have tough requirements on conference establishment time.
tldr.mechanism: The client puts a URI list in a 'recipient-list' body of its first INVITE to the conference factory URI and adds the 'recipient-list-invite' option-tag to a Require header field. The server creates the conference and invites everyone on the list.
tldr.outcome: Conference creation and the initial invitations happen in one operation. A 200 (OK) response says the conference exists and the list was understood, not that the invitees joined.

today: RFC 5366 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 4579, RFC 5363 and RFC 5364.

sections.title: The Problem: Slow Conference Setup
sections.content:
RFC 4579 describes how to create an ad hoc conference: the client sends an INVITE to a conference factory URI and gets the real conference URI back in the Contact header field of a response, typically a 200 (OK). That URI carries the isfocus feature tag. Only after that can the client add participants.

Some environments have tough requirements on conference establishment time. They need the User Agent Client (UAC) to request the conference and supply the initial participants in a single operation. This RFC meets that need using the mechanism for carrying URI lists in SIP messages from RFC 5363.
sections.eli5: Normally you first open a meeting room and then phone each guest. Here you hand over the guest list when you ask for the room, so the guests are rung right away.

sections.title: What the Client Does
sections.content:
A UAC that wants to include the initial participants in its first INVITE adds a body whose disposition type is recipient-list, as defined in RFC 5363. The body holds a URI list of the people the server should invite. The UAC MUST also put the recipient-list-invite option-tag in a Require header field, and it sends the INVITE to the conference factory URI.

The same INVITE transaction still carries the offer/answer exchange that sets up the session between the UAC and the server, so the request may hold a multipart body: a session description and a URI list.

The response status code says nothing about whether the server managed to bring the listed users in. A 200 (OK) means the conference was created, the UAC is in it, and the server understood the URI list. To learn about other users, the UAC SHOULD use general conference mechanisms such as the conference package from RFC 4575.
sections.eli5: You ask for the room and attach your guest list. The answer 'OK' only means the room is ready and your list was read, not that every guest has shown up.

sections.title: The URI-List Document Format
sections.content:
The default format for recipient-list bodies is the XML resource list format of RFC 4826, extended with the copy control attributes of RFC 5364. Conferencing UACs that generate such bodies and conference servers that handle them MUST support both, and MAY support other formats.

Each URI can carry a copyControl attribute set to to, cc or bcc, saying in what role the recipient gets the INVITE. A URI can also carry the anonymize attribute so the server does not disclose it to others.

Resource lists allow hierarchical lists and entries by reference to an XCAP root URI, which a conference does not need. UACs SHOULD therefore send flat lists and SHOULD NOT use <entry-ref> elements. A server receiving more than that MAY discard the extra information.
sections.eli5: The guest list is a simple list, one name per line. Each name can be marked 'main guest', 'copied guest' or 'secret guest', and some names can be hidden from the others.

sections.title: What the Conference Server Does
sections.content:
A server that can process INVITEs with a recipient-list body SHOULD include the recipient-list-invite option-tag in a Supported header field when responding to OPTIONS requests. When such an INVITE arrives, the server MUST follow the rules of RFC 4579 to create the ad hoc conference. It then SHOULD try to add the listed participants as if they had been added by any of the RFC 4579 methods. After that it behaves as a regular conference server.

If the list has entries with copyControl set to to or cc, the server SHOULD include a URI list in each outgoing INVITE. When it does, it MUST set Content-Disposition to recipient-list-history with a handling parameter of optional. It MUST follow RFC 5364 for the anonymize, count and copyControl attributes.
sections.eli5: The organizer opens the room, then phones each guest and tells them who else was invited, leaving out the secret guests and hiding the names marked private.

sections.title: Re-INVITEs Do Not Carry Lists
sections.content:
Once the dialog exists, the UAC can send re-INVITE requests, for example to change the media. Lists in re-INVITEs have no defined meaning for now, so UACs SHOULD NOT include recipient-list bodies in them.

A re-INVITE goes to the URI the server supplied in its Contact header field, not to the factory URI. If a server receives a re-INVITE with a recipient-list body, standard SIP procedures make it reject the request with a 420 (Bad Extension) carrying an Unsupported header field that lists recipient-list-invite. The conference URI does not support the extension; only the factory URI does.
sections.eli5: The guest list only works when you first ask for the room. Once you are inside, handing over another list does nothing and is turned away.

sections.title: A Worked Example
sections.content:
The RFC's example has a UAC send INVITE F1 to the factory with a multipart/mixed body: an application/sdp part and an application/resource-lists+xml part with the recipient-list disposition. The server answers with a 200 (OK) and sends its own INVITE to each listed user agent server (F3, F4, F5), each with SDP and a manipulated list.

The outgoing lists differ from the original. URIs tagged anonymize are replaced by sip:anonymous@anonymous.invalid with a count attribute giving how many were hidden, and URIs tagged bcc are removed.
sections.eli5: Alice sends one request with seven names. Each guest gets a call that shows only the names they are allowed to see, and the hidden ones show up as 'someone anonymous'.

sections.title: Security
sections.content:
Conferences usually have authorization rules about who may join and what media may be used. The RFC says such rules RECOMMENDED be used, and that the focus needs to authenticate potential participants with normal SIP mechanisms such as Digest authentication and certificates.

A conference server that sends INVITEs to a list acts as a URI-list service, so implementations that handle lists MUST follow the security rules in RFC 5363. These include opt-in lists and mandatory authentication and authorization of clients.
sections.eli5: A server that rings many people for you must check that you are allowed to ask, and that the people agreed to be rung, so nobody can use it to annoy others.

sections.title: The Option-Tag
sections.content: The RFC defines one new SIP option-tag, recipient-list-invite, registered in the Option Tags subregistry of the SIP parameter registry. Its description is that the body contains a list of URIs that indicates the recipients of the SIP INVITE request.
sections.eli5: It is a special label on the request that tells the server 'this call has a guest list attached'.

messages.label: F1 INVITE
messages.note: SDP plus URI list, sent to the factory URI.

messages.label: F3, F4, F5 INVITE
messages.note: SDP plus a manipulated URI list.
